title: FOSFORMEN : Randomized, multicenter, non-inferiority trial comparing the efficacy of fosfomycin versus fluoroquinolones or cotrimoxazole as oral follow-up treatment in febrile urinary tract infections in men caused by susceptible enterobacteria
official: FOSFORMEN : Randomized, multicenter, non-inferiority trial comparing the efficacy of fosfomycin versus fluoroquinolones or cotrimoxazole as oral follow-up treatment in febrile urinary tract infections in men caused by susceptible enterobacteria
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that the fosfomycin-trometamol (FT) combination  is not inferior to fluoroquinolones (FQ) or cotrimoxazole (TMP-SMX) as oral step-down therapy in febrile male urinary tract infections caused by Escherichia coli.
conditions: Febrile male urinary tract infections caused by Escherichia coli
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male
2. Age ≥ 18
3. Body temperature ≥ 38°C within the 72 hours preceding the diagnosis of UTI
4. At least one of the following symptoms : dysuria, higher urinary frequency, urgency, hematuria, suprapubic pain, prostatic pain, flank pain, or perineal pain
5. Positive urine microbiological examination (urine culture) : Sample collected before initiation of the empiric antibiotic therapy, ≥ 10 leukocytes/µL, and monomicrobial culture positive for E. coli with bacteriuria ≥ 103 CFU/mL
6. The strain must be suceptible to fosfomycin and to either FQ or TMP-SMX according to EUCAST
7. The strain must be suceptible to the empiric antibiotic therapy received
8. Ability to take oral treatment
9. Favorable clinical evolution after receiving effective empiric antibiotic therapy for 72 ± 24 hours ; favorable evolution is defined as body temperature < 38°C with clinical improvement of urinary tract infection signs and symptomps present at diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of another condition that could explain the fever
2. UTI treated within the past 3 months
3. High probability of death within 3 months
4. Major cognitive disorders
5. Patients deprived of their liberty by judicial or administrative decision, under guardianship or curatorship
6. Lack of social security coverage
7. Absence of written informed consent
8. Participation in another interventional research protocol
9. Individuals depreived of liberty by juriducal or administrative decision
10. Septic shock of urinary origin
11. Need for a urological procedure
12. Anatomical abnormalities of the urinary tract (e.g., urinary prostheses and implants [except JJ], Bricker, neobladder, total prostatectomy, uretrestomy, nephrostomy, urinary fistula)
13. Presence of an indwelling urinary catheter, except of placed during the current UTI episode
14. Neurogenic bladder
15. Immunosupression
16. Contraindication to the use of FQ, TMP-SMX or FT
17. Severe chronic kidney disease with an estimated flomerular filtration rate < 20 mL/min
